record.text: Baidu unveils ERNIE Bot at a pre-recorded Beijing event, with access limited to invited testers. It says 650 companies have signed up. Hong Kong shares fall as much as 10%.

Baidu opens ERNIE Bot to the general public on the day Chinese approvals under the generative-AI measures were reported. It is among the first approved firms, and the app tops the App Store free chart within 12 hours.
At Baidu World, Baidu unveils ERNIE 4.0, which Robin Li says is 'not inferior in any aspect to GPT-4'. It is open to invited users only, with enterprise API access by application.

On the Q3 2023 earnings call, Li says Baidu's chip stockpile covers the near term, then alternatives and in-house chips. He warns that the difficulty of getting advanced chips 'inevitably will have an impact on the pace of AI development in China'.
In an internal speech reported on 12-15 April, Li says open-source LLMs 'make little sense' and that closed source is needed for a viable business.

Baidu AI Cloud makes ERNIE Speed and ERNIE Lite free for all business users. They had cost 0.003-0.008 yuan per 1,000 tokens. The move comes hours after Alibaba's cut of up to 97%, in a price war that DeepSeek-V2 and ByteDance set off.
In a WeChat post, Baidu says ERNIE Bot, including premium features, will be free on desktop and mobile from 1 April. Press widely frames this as a response to DeepSeek.
Baidu commits to open-sourcing the ERNIE 4.5 series from 30 June, reversing Li's closed-source stance.
Baidu Search announces it will fully integrate DeepSeek-R1 alongside ERNIE, and adds DeepSeek to its developer platform.
On the Q4 2024 earnings call, Li credits DeepSeek for the open-source decision.
Baidu releases ERNIE 4.5 and the reasoning model ERNIE X1, which it claims matches DeepSeek-R1 at half the price. It makes ERNIE Bot free ahead of the 1 April schedule.
At Baidu Create, Baidu launches ERNIE 4.5 Turbo (80% cheaper, priced at 40% of DeepSeek-V3) and X1 Turbo (50% cheaper, about 25% of R1's price).

In the same keynote, Li credits DeepSeek but calls it 'slow and expensive' and prone to hallucination compared with mainstream Chinese models. This comes from Chinese media accounts; no transcript was found.

Li says Baidu has switched on a cluster of 30,000 third-generation Kunlun P800 chips. He says it can train DeepSeek-like models with hundreds of billions of parameters. This comes 10 days after the US made H20 licences indefinite.
On the Q1 2025 call, VP Shen Dou says domestic chips and software give a 'strong foundation for long-term innovation' that will shield Baidu's AI push from US curbs on the H20.
Baidu open-sources the ERNIE 4.5 family on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, built on PaddlePaddle, on the date it committed to in February.
Apollo Go signs a multi-year deal with Uber to deploy thousands of robotaxis outside the US and mainland China, starting in Asia and the Middle East.
Apollo Go and Lyft announce robotaxi deployment in Europe, with Germany and the UK first from 2026, pending regulatory approval.
At Baidu World, Baidu previews ERNIE 5.0, a 2.4-trillion-parameter natively omni-modal model. It is proprietary with no weights, a move back from the open release of ERNIE 4.5.
Baidu publishes a five-year Kunlun chip roadmap: M100 for inference in early 2026, M300 for training in early 2027, Tianchi supernodes, and a one-million-card cluster by 2030.

exam.scored_on: exact verb match against the real later action, normalized by the actor's own consistency over time.
baselines: always the actor's most common verb (majority baseline)

hidden_test.text: Baidu discloses that its chip unit Kunlunxin filed confidentially for a Hong Kong IPO on 1 January. Baidu will stay the controlling shareholder. Press frames the move as riding China's self-reliance push amid US controls.
ERNIE 5.0 leaves preview and becomes the official version. It stays proprietary, with no weights and only a later technical report on 6 February. On 15 January it had ranked #8 globally on LMArena.
In a TIME interview, Li plays down open source and US chip limits while admitting China lags by generations.

In the same interview, Li backs light-touch regulation. He also says 'I'm not so worried about the restrictions on the chip' and that China is 'probably two, three generations behind the U.S.' on accelerators.

After more than 100 Apollo Go robotaxis stall in Wuhan on the evening of 31 March, Baidu issues no official statement. Customer service blames 'network issues', police cite a system failure, and operations resume.
Baidu releases ERNIE 5.1, claiming leading performance at 6% of comparable pre-training cost. The preview had ranked #1 Chinese model on LMArena on 30 April.

Q2 2026 results report Apollo Go starting fully driverless commercial service in Dubai (also on Uber) and getting Hong Kong's first fully driverless test permits. They also report London testing with Uber and Lyft, Switzerland with PostBus, and a Kazakhstan MoU. Li cites 'strengthening its safety and operational capabilities'.
